posts.title: The Sound Of A Good Deed.
posts.description: The sound of a good deed. I’m on the fence about writing this blog post. Not because it’s too risqué or too revealing but because, as I sit here looking at a blank screen, it doesn’t feel like it’s going to go anywhere. So, if you want to scroll away from this right now, be my guest. You probably won’t miss much. Here’s the boring thing that happened earlier today that for some reason, I feel compelled to write about: a gardener holding a leaf-blower walked by me as I tossed recycling in into the communal bins by the side of the building. I nodded to him and said my typical, “What’s up man?” He nodded back and kept waking. His yellow t-shirt was stained with sweat and shards of cut grass were clumped to the side of his head. It felt like 400 degrees out. I walked behind him towards my car. I was holding a can of grapefruit seltzer which was still cold from my fridge. posts.title: Here’s Me At The Eiffel Tower
posts.description: I miss being around people I love and people who love me. I miss the feeling of family. I miss it so much. That automatic, taken for granted, these-are-my-people, no matter what, through thick or thin, come rain or come shine-extensions-of-myself. And I didn’t really realize this until tonight. Context: Earlier this evening, on a whim, I went to dinner at Ben’s Deli in Boca Raton. By myself as usual. The one on Long Island was a place we’d go fairly often. Me. My mom and dad. Sister. Brother-in-law. Nephews. And maybe someone I was dating at any of those times. It’s been at least a decade since those days and seeing all of those crowded tables tonight made me miss it all so thoroughly. The end. Thanks for reading. I know it’s too abrupt to just stop on a dime like that, but nothing else needs to be said. I’ve already said too much by saying anything at all. posts.title: Then And Now Is Now
posts.description: Sometimes, when I was a small boy, my dad would gently and lovingly stretch my limbs early in the morning soon after waking up. He’d sit on the side of my bed and pull my arms. Then pull my legs. And then give my torso a tiny twist as if he was making taffy. Playful sounds of exertion from his mouth. Loosening my little joints. Helping me grow. We’d both smile. My mom would be sitting there too. Smiling. This memory arose from the backlogs of my being while I watched my cat wake up from a nap. He saw me standing over him and his eyes grew big for a moment. But he quickly relaxed and proceeded to stretch his little body from the top of his black and white head down to his perfectly pink toe beans. “Good stretch,” I said. And then, in case he’d like a little assistance, I gave him a tender tug in opposite directions. Playfully making sounds of exertion.
